youtube.aciklama:
How is consent obtained in audiology, and how is health data protected? In this lesson we learn the elements of informed consent, parental consent for children, Türkiye's Patient Rights Regulation, the Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK), and what to watch for when sharing records and images. This is not legal advice; check the current legislation.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698, KVKK (Official Gazette, April 7, 2016, No. 29677; Article 6 as amended by Law No. 7499); Patient Rights Regulation (Official Gazette, August 1, 1998, No. 23420); Beauchamp TL, Childress JF. Principles of Biomedical Ethics; ASHA, Code of Ethics (2023).

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will learn the elements of informed consent and parental consent for children.

cumleler.yazi: Then we will look at protecting health data and sharing records under Türkiye's Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698.
cumleler.ses: Then we will look at protecting health data and sharing records under Türkiye's Personal Data Protection Law number sixty-six ninety-eight.

cumleler: Informed consent is the permission a patient gives freely after being informed about a procedure.
The first element is information: the procedure, its purpose, possible risks and options are explained clearly.
The second is understanding; giving information is not enough, we check that the patient has truly understood.
The third is decision-making capacity: the person must be able to weigh the information and reach a conclusion.
The fourth is voluntariness; consent is given without pressure, threats or deception.
The last element is the decision itself: the patient may accept, refuse, or change their mind later.

maddeler.metin: How it is done, how long

cumleler.yazi: In Türkiye, informing patients and obtaining their consent is governed by the 1998 Patient Rights Regulation.
cumleler.ses: In Türkiye, informing patients and obtaining their consent is governed by the nineteen ninety-eight Patient Rights Regulation.

cumleler: Article 15 of the Regulation lists what must be explained; the possible causes of the disease and its likely course are among them.
How the procedure is done and how long it will take are also explained; for example, preparing for a test done during sleep.
Possible complications and discomforts are stated clearly; for example, that the caloric test may cause brief dizziness.
Other diagnostic and treatment options are explained, with their benefits and risks.
The possible consequences of refusing the proposed procedure are also part of the information.
The Regulation asks that information be given as simply as possible, in a way the patient can understand.
The consent process begins with introducing yourself by name and title and stating the purpose of the visit.
Then the tests to be done, how long they take and any discomfort are explained in plain language.
The patient's questions are answered, and they are asked to summarize what they heard in their own words.
For routine, risk-free tests, consent is often verbal; for procedures the institution specifies, a written consent form is used.
That consent was obtained, who gave the information, and any reservations the patient has are noted in the file.
Consent is a process, not a moment of signing; the patient may withdraw consent even during a procedure.
Under Article 24 of the Patient Rights Regulation, if the patient is a minor or under guardianship, a parent or guardian gives permission.
The same article provides that a minor patient able to understand should also be heard and take part in the decision.
So the test is explained to the child in age-appropriate language and their agreement is sought; this is called the child's assent.
Steps such as putting on headphones or placing a probe can first be shown on a toy or on the mother.
In divorced or separated families, the legal authority of the person giving consent is verified under the institution's rules.
If the child comes with a grandparent or another relative, how parental consent will be obtained is clarified in advance.
For an adult whose decision-making capacity is in doubt, the role of a legal representative is set by the institution's rules.
For a patient who does not speak Turkish, an independent interpreter is preferred over a family member when possible.
For a Deaf patient who uses sign language, a sign language interpreter is a condition of equal information.
For every patient with hearing loss, spoken explanation is supported with a written summary, pictures and a quiet room.
Taking part in research is separate from a clinical procedure; the Regulation requires written consent for medical research.

ogeler.metin: Cannot be linked to a person

cumleler.yazi: Türkiye's Personal Data Protection Law, known by its Turkish abbreviation KVKK, was published in 2016 as Law No. 6698.
cumleler.ses: Türkiye's Personal Data Protection Law, known by its Turkish abbreviation KVKK, was published in twenty sixteen as Law number sixty-six ninety-eight.

cumleler: Under the Law, personal data is any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
Explicit consent is consent on a specific matter, based on information and given freely.
The natural or legal person who sets the purposes and means of processing and runs the record system is called the data controller.
Anonymized data is data that cannot be linked to a person, even when matched with other data.
An audiogram kept together with a name and national ID number is clearly personal data.
This lesson is general educational content, not legal advice; laws can change, so always check the current legislation.

maddeler.metin: May be processed for diagnosis, treatment

cumleler: Article 6 of the Law lists health data as special category, or sensitive, personal data.
Biometric and genetic data are in the same group; results of genetic hearing loss tests are covered too.

cumleler.yazi: This article was amended in 2024, and the conditions under which special category data may be processed were listed anew.
cumleler.ses: This article was amended in twenty twenty-four, and the conditions under which special category data may be processed were listed anew.

cumleler: One condition is processing the data to carry out medical diagnosis, treatment and care services.
Processing for this purpose is done by persons under a duty of confidentiality, or by authorized institutions.
Using the same data for another purpose, such as promotion, teaching slides or social media, needs a separate legal basis.
For details and exceptions, check the current text of the Law and the decisions of the Personal Data Protection Board.
Article 10 of the Law gives the data controller a duty to inform; first, the identity of the data controller is stated.
Then the purpose for which personal data will be processed is explained.
It also says to whom, and for what purpose, the data may be transferred; for example, the reimbursement agency or a physician.
The method of collecting the data and its legal basis are also part of the notice.
Finally, the person is told their rights under the Law and how to apply.
Informing and explicit consent are different: informing is done when data is collected, explicit consent is obtained only when required.
Under Article 11 of the Law, a person can apply to the data controller to learn whether their data is processed.
If it is, they can request information about it, the purpose of processing and the third parties it was transferred to.
They can ask for incomplete or wrongly processed data to be corrected; for example, a wrongly entered date of birth.
When the Law's conditions are met, they can ask for the data to be erased or destroyed; health records also have separate retention rules.
If they suffer harm from unlawful processing, they can claim compensation for that harm.
Every staff member should know how their institution responds to these applications, and who is responsible.
Privacy is protected not only in files, but also in the booth, in the hallway and on the screen.
Taking a history with the booth door closed is much safer than talking in the waiting room.
The computer screen is placed so that the next patient cannot see it.
Audiograms, otoscopy images and photos of the patient are not taken on a personal phone.
If images are needed for teaching or a scientific talk, identifying details are removed and the institution's approval process is followed.
On social media, a patient image or a recognizable case history should be weighed very carefully, even with explicit consent.

maddeler.metin: Access only for those who need it
Paper records in a locked cabinet

cumleler: Article 12 of the Law requires the data controller to take technical and administrative measures for an appropriate level of security.
Each staff member logs in to the audiometer software and the patient record system with their own password; passwords are not shared.
The screen is locked when leaving the computer; an open session lets someone else reach the data.
Each staff member accesses only the data they need for their work; this is known as the principle of least privilege.
Results are shared through the institution's secure systems, not through personal messaging apps.
Paper forms and old audiograms are kept in a locked cabinet and destroyed under the institution's rules.

sahneler.metin: Before sending results to a patient, verify identity and contact details; do not share results with a caller until you know who they are.
cumleler: A tip from the field: do not immediately give information to someone who calls and asks about a patient's results.
Verify, in the way the institution specifies, that the caller is the patient or is authorized.
When sending a report, double-check the email address and recipient; a report sent to the wrong person cannot be taken back.
When unsure, give the result to the patient in person, or through the institution's secure channel.

maddeler.metin: Health data is special category data

cumleler: Informed consent rests on information, understanding, decision-making capacity and voluntariness, and it is a process.
For a minor, a parent's or guardian's permission is obtained; the child is also heard and informed by level of understanding.

cumleler.yazi: The KVKK, Law No. 6698, treats health data as special category personal data and ties its processing to strict conditions.
cumleler.ses: The KVKK, Law number sixty-six ninety-eight, treats health data as special category personal data and ties its processing to strict conditions.

cumleler: The data controller informs people and takes security measures; images and records are not shared beyond their purpose.

sahneler.aciklama: An audiogram is health data; for teaching, _identifying details are removed_ and the institution's process is followed.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: a trainee wants to post on social media an audiogram showing the patient's name, as an interesting case. Is this appropriate?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: no; identifying details must be removed and the institution's approval process followed.
An audiogram with a name is special category personal data; sharing from a personal account carries both ethical and legal risk.
